Net transactions, US$ Millions. Fiscal quarters plotted at quarter start (Q1 = Apr–Jun).

Exports of major commodities, US$ Millions, fiscal years plotted at April of the first year. All 31 published commodity groups are baked (series ordered by the latest year's value); the published Total Exports row is kept in crosscheck and the groups sum to it within $1mn. The total matches the monthly customs series (rbi-trade) summed over the fiscal year to well under 0.5%.

End-of-quarter external debt stocks by sector, ₹ Crore (this table is published in rupees only; the annual end-March US$ series is rbi-debt). Calendar quarter-ends plotted at March/June/September/December.
End-March stocks plotted at March. Composition by source in US$ Millions; ratios as published.

Monthly average exchange rates, ₹ per unit of foreign currency. Yen is ₹ per single yen in this ingest (the source's unit field is empty; the RBI's usual per-100-yen convention would read ~100× higher). Euro begins Jan 1999.
Reserves are total foreign exchange reserves, US$ Millions. USD/INR is the monthly average rate, ₹ per US$.

USD/INR forward premia (inter-bank, monthly average), per cent per annum by tenor. Negative values (dollar at a forward discount) occur briefly, e.g. late 2003. 1-month begins Jun 1995 (3/6-month in Mar 1993); missing months are as published.

Turnover in the foreign exchange market: gross purchases plus sales in the month, US$ Millions (the source's unit field is empty; the scale matches the RBI's published USD-million turnover tables). Total is computed as merchant + inter-bank and cross-checked against the published Grand Total — they agree within $2mn everywhere except September 2018, where the published Grand Total exceeds the segment sum by ~$62bn in the source itself; the discrepancy is the source's, kept as published.

RBI sale/purchase of US dollars, US$ Millions. Gross legs are positive; net is purchases minus sales; the forward book is the end-of-month outstanding position, sales negative. Months the source leaves blank ("-", typically no operations) are nulls, not zeros.

Net invisibles by category, US$ Millions; fiscal years plotted at April of the first year. Chosen to tell the services/remittances story: total invisibles, non-factor services, miscellaneous services (the software/business-services carrier — no separate software line exists in this table), income (persistently negative), and private transfers i.e. remittances. The source's Receipts/GDP and Payments/GDP rows are mislabelled gross levels and are not baked.
US$ Millions. Outstandings are stocks; flows are net inflows(+) / outflows(-) in the month.
Levels, US$ Millions. Broad commodity composition of merchandise trade.

Direction of foreign trade: exports to and imports from the sixteen largest partner countries, US$ Millions, fiscal years plotted at April of the first year. The source labels the United Kingdom's rows "USA" (its countries dimension has no UK); the two values are separated by size — the larger is the United States in every year, verified against the RBI's published bilateral series — and the build fails if the pair ever overlaps. This table's totals differ from the monthly customs series (rbi-trade) by up to ~0.3% — different compilation of the same trade; both totals are kept in crosscheck.
Levels, US$ Millions. Balance is computed (exports − imports) and cross-checked against the published Trade Balance.
